title: Aram's first-use notes
subtitle: Decision walkthrough · 11 Nov 2026 · findings from Aram · narrated by Duo's house voice
posterLine: What Aram found on first use, what's true in the code, then five decisions. Tap play and listen; it stops when it needs you.
footer: Findings from Aram's first-use notes. Built with the decision-walkthrough skill from docs/research/aram-feedback-walkthrough/spec.json. Answers are saved in this page and sent to director-duo-v2.

lines.text: This one starts with Aram. He's been using Duo, and he sent you his first-use notes.
His big one is onboarding. He knows he's underusing Duo. He can't tell how to start a director, or how tasks differ from sessions.

Then five smaller ones. Sometimes Duo is a white IDE, and sometimes a terminal. The file list should fold. The right side should hide. File names in replies should be clickable. And the menu spells colour with a U.
I checked each one against today's code. Every finding in here is his.
Most of what Aram asked for is already built, and he couldn't find it.
The right side hides, with ⌥⌘0 or a toolbar button. It just isn't in the View menu.
Folders fold. The Files section doesn't, and Duo forgets which folders were open.
File names in replies are already links that open on the right. But only in chat mode.
That's the root of it. Home opens in chat, but a new project session opens in the terminal. So Duo looks like two apps, and his had no links.
And the guide and the films exist, but Help links to neither.
You asked about conventions for Claude. So first I tested what it writes with none. Four Haiku turns, in a scratch project.
Unprompted, it wrote every file as a path from the project folder, in backticks, with the line number.
Chat's link rule caught three of the five.
It missed two. A name with no extension, and a path with a space in it.
Then I gave Claude a rule to write those two differently. Nothing changed.
So the fix belongs in Duo. A backticked name that's a real file becomes a link, and a command click in the terminal opens in Duo too.
You also asked how Legacy Duo told Claude it was inside Duo. Five ways at once.
A wrapper around the claude command added a priming file to the system prompt, and a hook in your own settings printed it again.
Its one rule about showing things was, after you create a file, reveal it.
Duo v2 starts Claude itself. So it passes a short, generated primer at every session start, and touches none of your files.
The primer already says you're inside Duo. It doesn't say file names are links, or when to open one. And Claude is never told which view you're in.

chapters.title: A new user's first session
chapters.ask: Which mode should a new user's first project session open in?
chapters.why: Chat is where replies are formatted and file names are links. New installs start in the terminal today.

look.label: Research · 1.1 White IDE or terminal wrapper

lines.text: First decision. Which mode should a new user's first session open in?
Today it's the mode used last, and that starts as terminal.

options.label: Chat, for new installs
options.desc: Existing users keep the mode used last.

lines.text: I'd start new installs in chat. Formatted replies, clickable files, and the pill becomes the way out to the terminal. Nobody's current setup changes.

options.label: Keep terminal first, and teach the pill
options.desc: A tooltip, a Session menu item, an explainer.

lines.text: Or keep terminal first, and teach it, with a tooltip, a menu item and an explainer. A new user still starts without links.

options.label: Ask on the first session
options.desc: A new question; needs a design.

lines.text: Or ask, chat or terminal, on the first session. That's a question before any value, and it needs a design.

chapters.title: Onboarding: what first
chapters.ask: What onboarding should be built first?
chapters.why: Aram's main note. The app has no welcome, one explainer, and no link to the guide or the films.

lines.text: Next, Aram's main note, onboarding. What to build first?
Today Help has four items, one feature has an explainer, and there's no welcome.

options.label: The no-new-design layer now, a designed welcome next
options.desc: Help links, guide pages, three explainers; then a canvas round for the welcome.

lines.text: I'd build what needs no new design now. Help links to the guide and both films, guide pages for the director and the two modes, and three more explainers. Then design a first-run welcome on the canvas.

options.label: The welcome first
options.desc: The best first minute; waits on a canvas round.

lines.text: Or design the welcome first. It's the best first minute, but the cheap fixes wait on a canvas round.

options.label: A Meet Duo sample project
options.desc: About a week, and it has to stay true as Duo changes.

lines.text: Or a sample project to poke at. That's about a week, and it has to stay true as Duo changes.

chapters.title: Starting the director
chapters.ask: How should a user start the director?
chapters.why: Aram couldn't tell how. Today you type it, and the guide has no page on it.

lines.text: Aram's example was the director. How should someone start one?
Today you type, be the director, in a session. It works, and nobody would guess it.

options.label: Project › Start Director, plus an explainer
options.desc: On duo2 director start, which already exists.

lines.text: I'd add Start Director to the Project menu, on the verb that already exists, plus an explainer.

options.label: Also an empty director slot in the sidebar
options.desc: Most discoverable; a new mark on an approved screen, so a canvas round.

lines.text: Or also draw an empty director slot at the top of the sidebar. It's the most discoverable, and it needs the canvas first.

options.label: Only teach the phrase
options.desc: A guide page and an explainer; no new control.

lines.text: Or only teach the phrase, in the guide and an explainer.

chapters.title: What Duo tells Claude
chapters.ask: What more should Duo tell Claude about being inside Duo?
chapters.why: Aram wants files to show up on the right. Only Claude can open one without a click.

lines.text: What more should Duo tell Claude?
The primer is the right place. It's rebuilt with every version, and it touches none of your files.

options.label: One sentence, and fix the links in Duo
options.desc: File names are links; open a finished document with duo2 doc open.

lines.text: I'd add one sentence. File names in replies are links, and when you finish a document, open it for the user. That's the part only Claude can do. The file shows up on the right, with no click.

options.label: Fix the links in Duo only

lines.text: Or tell Claude nothing new. Files are clickable, but they never open by themselves.

options.label: A fuller convention, per mode
options.desc: Chat and terminal variants, sent again when the view changes.

lines.text: Or a fuller convention, with chat and terminal variants. It costs tokens, goes stale when you switch views, and in the test Claude ignored the finer rule.

chapters.title: Colour or Color
chapters.ask: Should the menu say Window Colour or Window Color?
chapters.why: Aram's nit. The app says Colour; macOS beside it says Color on a US Mac.

look.label: Research · 1.5 Window Colour in the menu

lines.text: Last one, and it's Aram's nit. The menu says Window Colour, with a U.
Those six strings are the app's only use of either spelling, and macOS beside it says Color.

options.label: Window Color
options.desc: US spelling in the app's own words; duo2 window colour stays as an alias.

lines.text: I'd use American spelling in the app's own words, and keep the old verb working.

options.label: Keep Window Colour
options.desc: Matches the docs; reads as a typo on a US Mac.

lines.text: Or keep it. It matches the docs, and it reads as a typo on a US Mac.

options.label: Localize both
options.desc: en-GB and en-US; a lot of machinery for six strings.

lines.text: Or localize for both. Correct, and a lot of machinery for six strings.
That's all five.
The link fixes, the pane controls and the teaching layer need no decision, so they're logged as builds.
Thanks to Aram for the notes. There's a reply drafted for him in the research doc.
